title: Construction Debris Removal for Contractors: Costs, Virginia Rules and Dumpster vs. Haul-Off

contentHtml:
Construction debris removal costs $300 to $1,000 on average, according to HomeGuide. Angi's 2026 data puts the average job at about $450. Most haulers price by how much of the truck your debris fills, and heavy loads like concrete or brick cost more.

This guide is for contractors, remodelers and homeowners in the middle of a renovation. It covers national prices, what Virginia counts as construction waste, when a dumpster makes sense, and the asbestos and lead steps to plan for before the walls come down.

Construction debris removal cost by truck load

National averages by truck volume:

Truck volume usedHomeGuide averageAngi average
1/4 truck$300 to $500$100 to $300
1/2 truck$400 to $600$200 to $400
3/4 truck$500 to $800$300 to $600
Full truck$700 to $1,000$500 to $800

The two sources differ, so treat these as a range to compare quotes against, not a local price. Mr Demo Pro quotes construction debris removal by volume, material mix and access, so you know the cost before the crew arrives. Estimates are free.

What changes the price

  • Volume: the more truck space the pile takes, the higher the price.
  • Material mix: concrete, brick, tile and metal weigh far more than lumber or drywall. Some haulers charge heavy loads by weight.
  • Access: stairs, upper floors, tight driveways and active job sites add labor time.
  • Prep: debris already broken down and piled near the driveway loads faster than debris spread through a house.
  • Special materials: paint, solvents, appliances and anything with asbestos need separate handling and can add fees. Angi puts typical hazardous waste fees at $150 to $300.

Dumpster rental vs. load-and-haul

HomeGuide puts dumpster rental at $220 to $780 per week. A dumpster works well on a long project that makes steady waste, as long as you have room for the container and a crew to fill it.

Load-and-haul is usually the better fit when:

  • The dumpster is full, late or the wrong size for the phase
  • There is no space for a container in the driveway or on the street
  • Your crew's time is worth more on the build than on loading
  • You need the area cleared at the end of a phase so the next trade can start

Many Mr Demo Pro customers prefer full-service load-and-haul. If a container makes more sense for your timeline, say so when you request a quote and we will recommend the best approach.

What counts as construction debris in Virginia

Virginia's solid waste regulations (9VAC20-81-10) define construction waste as material from building, remodeling or repairing structures. That includes:

  • Lumber, wire and sheetrock
  • Broken brick, shingles and glass
  • Pipes, concrete and paving materials
  • Metal and plastics that were part of the construction, plus empty containers for those materials

The same definition excludes paints, coatings, solvents, asbestos, liquids, compressed gases and garbage. Keep those out of the debris pile. Household furniture and general clutter fit better under junk removal or a cleanout.

Where it goes, and where it can't

Under 9VAC20-81-110, permitted construction/demolition/debris (CDD) landfills may accept demolition, construction and debris waste. Local drop-off rules can be tighter. SPSA transfer stations, for example, only take rigid items like construction material up to six feet long and six inches across.

Dumping debris on public property or on private land without the owner's written consent is a misdemeanor in Virginia. Under Va. Code § 33.2-802, it carries a fine of $500 to $2,500, up to 12 months in jail, or both. When you hire a hauler, ask where the load goes.

Plan for asbestos and lead before demolition

Asbestos inspections

In Virginia, a building department will not issue a permit to renovate or demolish a building first permitted before January 1, 1985, until the owner certifies that the affected areas were inspected for asbestos by a licensed inspector (Va. Code § 36-99.7). The rule does not apply to single-family homes or buildings with four or fewer units, unless the work is for commercial or public development. If an inspection finds asbestos, a licensed abatement contractor handles it before general demolition and debris removal.

Lead paint in pre-1978 homes

Renovations in homes built before 1978 fall under the EPA's lead renovation, repair and painting rule. The EPA says lead-containing waste must be collected at the end of each work day, kept contained on site and contained during transport. Dumping and open burning of residential lead paint waste is not allowed.

How to keep debris from slowing the job

  1. Schedule load-outs by phase. Book haul-off for the end of demo, framing or punch list, not after the debris has piled up for weeks.
  2. Stage piles near access. A pile close to the driveway loads faster and costs less.
  3. Separate what can be recycled. Clean metal and concrete can often go somewhere other than a landfill. Ask your hauler how to sort.
  4. Keep hazardous items apart. Paint, solvents and suspect asbestos materials need their own plan.
  5. Protect finished areas. Clear a path from the work area to the truck before loading starts.

How Mr Demo Pro handles construction debris

  1. Share photos and access. Send pictures of the pile or rooms, note stairs or tight driveways, and tell us if the job is mid-renovation or final cleanup.
  2. Clear quote. We price by volume, material mix and access.
  3. Load and haul. The crew clears the debris, protects walkways where needed and loads everything for disposal.
  4. Site ready for the next phase. We leave the work area clear so contractors, inspectors or installers can move forward.

If the project also needs selective demolition of walls, floors or fixtures, we can combine interior demolition and haul-off so you are not managing two crews. See how we work with contractors and remodelers.

Construction debris removal FAQ

National averages run $300 to $1,000 per load, depending on volume, weight and access. Mr Demo Pro quotes each Hampton Roads job after photos or a quick on-site look, and estimates are free.

What is considered construction debris?

Drywall, lumber, flooring, tile, cabinets, fixtures, packaging and mixed remodel waste. Hazardous materials such as paint, solvents and asbestos need special handling and a separate plan.

Do you provide dumpsters?

Many customers prefer full-service load-and-haul instead of a dumpster. If a container makes more sense for your timeline, tell us when you request a quote and we will recommend the best approach.

Mr Demo Pro serves Yorktown, Norfolk, Newport News, Hampton, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake and nearby cities for renovation debris removal and contractor job-site cleanouts.
